report.summary: Chunk 4 of 11: defines probes 2 (instruction), 3 (anchoring), 4 (comprehension) with build/expect/check functions and helpers.
risks: check_anchoring | medium | Uses word set intersection which may be fooled by partial matches (e.g., 'twofold' matches 'two'). | Add word-boundary regex or exact matching.

claims.text: Strip TRANSPORT artefacts only -- never content.
claims.why: The function removes code fences, surrounding quotes, and whitespace; these are transport artefacts.

claims.text: Code fences, surrounding quotes and stray whitespace are things a CLI wrapper adds; removing them keeps the probe measuring instruction-following rather than punishing a lane for its own output framing.
claims.why: The function does exactly that removal.

claims.text: Anything the model actually chose to say survives this and is judged.
claims.why: Only transport artefacts are stripped; content remains unless it matches the patterns removed.

claims.text: It knew the answer and said more anyway. That is the degradation this probe exists for -- a lane that is alive and no longer obedient.
claims.why: The function returns 'not_exact' when expected string is present but not exact match.

claims.text: Detect a lane that copied the decoy instead of answering.
claims.why: The function returns 'anchored_on_decoy' if decoy word is found in reply.

claims.text: Reported as a QUALITY signal by PROBES: a model anchoring on a prior turn is alive, reachable and useless for reasoning work.
claims.why: The constant PROBES is not defined in this chunk; the claim about how it is reported cannot be verified.

claims.text: Calling that a liveness failure would page someone about a model choice; calling it nothing is how it went unnoticed for a day.
claims.why: This refers to operational behaviour not present in code.

claims.text: Decoy present WINS over a correct word also being present: a reply containing both is a reply that regurgitated the transcript.
claims.why: The function checks has_decoy first and returns immediately if true, so decoy wins.

observations.what: _normalise removes trailing dot with .rstrip('.') which may remove more than one dot.
check_instruction uses 'want in (reply or "")' which does not use normalized text; could cause false positives if non-normalized reply contains the expected string.
check_anchoring uses word set intersection which may match substrings (e.g., 'twofold' matches 'two').
_summaries is defined but chunk ends before its body completes; references _SUMMARY_DECOYS which is not defined in chunk.
